problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=\frac{1}{{t}^{3}},\,y=\frac{3}{t}.$ Given that $\frac{dy}{dx}={t}^{2},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$

feedback.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={e}^{2t},\,y={e}^{4t}.$ Given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2{e}^{2t},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=2{e}^{2t},$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({e}^{2t})=2{e}^{2t}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2{e}^{2t})}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
